title: Idli with Sambar & Chutney
steps: Prepare a fermented batter of rice and urad dal.
Steam the batter in idli molds for 10-12 minutes.
Prepare a tangy lentil sambar with tamarind and mixed vegetables.
Temper the sambar with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and red chillies.
Serve the hot idlis submerged or alongside the sambar.

fullIngredients.name: Toor dal, tamarind, mixed vegetables for sambar
Coconut, green chillies, curry leaves for chutney

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Puducherry versions may use less chilli heat.

title: Baguette or Croissant with Coffee
steps: Purchase or bake fresh, crusty French baguettes and flaky croissants.
Slice the baguette and toast lightly if desired.
Serve with a generous spread of butter and fruit jam.
Accompany with strong local filter coffee or French press coffee.
Enjoy a classic Franco-Pondicherrian morning meal.

fullIngredients.name: Filter coffee or café au lait

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Bakeries in the French Quarter maintain traditional recipes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Can be made fully plain for stricter diets.

title: Masala Dosa
steps: Spread fermented rice-lentil batter thinly on a hot greased tawa.
Cook until the bottom is crisp and golden brown.
Place a spiced potato masala filling in the center of the dosa.
Fold the edges over the filling.
Serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.

fullIngredients.name: Boiled potatoes, onion, mustard, curry leaves, turmeric for filling

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Some local spots serve egg dosa or meat-gravy variations.

title: Egg Dosa
steps: Spread dosa batter thinly on a hot tawa.
Crack an egg directly onto the cooking dosa and spread it evenly.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper, and chopped onions.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until the egg sets and dosa crisps.
Fold and serve hot.

fullIngredients.name: Side of sambar or light meat gravy

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Popular at places like Rolex and local tea shops.

title: Vegetable Poriyal & Rice Thali
steps: Chop mixed vegetables and parboil them.
Heat oil, temper with mustard seeds, urad dal, and curry leaves.
Add the vegetables and sauté briefly.
Garnish generously with freshly grated coconut.
Serve as part of a traditional South Indian thali with rice and rasam.

fullIngredients.name: Seasonal vegetables (beans, carrot, cabbage, etc.) for poriyal
Coconut, mustard, curry leaves, onion for tempering

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Banana-leaf service is still common in local restaurants.

title: Fish Assad Curry (Meen Assad)
steps: Marinate fish lightly with turmeric and salt.
Sauté onions, ginger, garlic, and green chillies.
Add thin coconut milk and gentle spices, bringing to a simmer.
Add the fish and cook until tender.
Finish with thick coconut milk and a squeeze of lemon.

fullIngredients.name: Fresh fish (seer, pomfret or local catch)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Often served with rice or appam.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Signature dish of Creole home cooking.

title: Meen Puyabaise
steps: Clean a variety of fresh seafood (fish, prawns, squid).
Prepare a base of onions, tomatoes, garlic, and a blend of French-Indian herbs/spices.
Add water or stock and simmer to create a flavorful broth.
Add the seafood and cook gently until just done.
Serve the bouillabaisse-style stew with crusty bread.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Best with very fresh coastal catch.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Still prepared in traditional Creole homes and select restaurants.

title: Kadugu Yerra (Mustard Prawn Curry)
steps: Clean fresh prawns and marinate lightly.
Prepare a robust paste of mustard seeds, chillies, and garlic.
Heat oil and sauté onions until translucent.
Add the mustard paste and the prawns.
Cook quickly on high heat until prawns are cooked and coated in the spicy masala.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, curry leaves, mild spices

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Pairs well with rice or appam.

title: Mutton Sambar
steps: Boil mutton pieces with turmeric until tender.
Cook toor dal until soft and mushy.
Prepare a tamarind-based broth with onions, tomatoes, and sambar powder.
Combine the cooked mutton, dal, and broth; simmer together.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves before serving.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A classic of Franco-Indian Catholic households.

title: Puducherry Egg Curry
steps: Hard-boil eggs, peel, and make shallow slits on them.
Prepare a rich onion-tomato gravy flavored with ginger, garlic, and garam masala.
Add coconut milk for a creamy texture.
Drop the boiled eggs into the simmering curry.
Cook for a few minutes so the eggs absorb the flavors.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Common in both home and restaurant menus.

title: Pondicherry-style Ratatouille
steps: Chop eggplant, zucchini, bell peppers, and tomatoes into even pieces.
Sauté onions and garlic in olive oil.
Add the vegetables and cook slowly until tender.
Season with a blend of French herbs (Herbes de Provence) and a pinch of local spice.
Serve warm as a side dish or with crusty bread.

fullIngredients.name: Eggplant, zucchini, tomato, bell pepper, onion
Olive oil or ghee, garlic, herbs
Optional mild spices or curry leaves

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Often the main vegetarian option in French-influenced restaurants.

title: Crepes (Sweet or Savoury)
steps: Prepare a thin, smooth batter of flour, eggs, milk, and a pinch of salt.
Pour a ladle of batter onto a hot, buttered crepe pan and swirl to coat.
Cook until lightly browned on one side, then flip.
Add sweet (sugar/lemon, Nutella) or savory (cheese/mushroom) fillings.
Fold and serve immediately.

fullIngredients.name: Flour, eggs, milk, butter for batter
Sweet fillings: sugar, chocolate, fruit jam

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A direct French colonial contribution still thriving.

title: Medu Vadai / Potato Vadai
steps: Soak urad dal and grind into a thick, fluffy batter with minimal water.
Mix in chopped onions, green chillies, ginger, curry leaves, and whole peppercorns.
Shape into small patties with a hole in the center.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot with coconut chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, ginger

title: Mutton Roll
steps: Cook minced mutton with onions, green chillies, and dry spices until dry.
Prepare thin wrappers from maida or use pre-made spring roll wrappers.
Place a spoonful of the spicy mutton filling on the wrapper and roll tightly, sealing the edges.
Deep-fry the rolls until crispy and golden.
Serve hot as an evening snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Widely available at street stalls and small eateries.
